compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`import rebar` callers get a return value, not a terminal, so the first-class way to raise
a non-fatal warning is Python's dedicated **`warnings`** subsystem (not `logging`, which is
silent unless the app configures it, and which the brainstorm explicitly rejected as "log
only"). This story emits a `warnings.warn` of a dedicated category from single-ticket
library functions when the detector fires.

Depends on the detector (`cross_session_warning_for`, sibling story) and the reducer
clearing.

## Approach

Define a dedicated warning category `class CrossSessionWarning(UserWarning)` (exported from
the package, e.g. `rebar.CrossSessionWarning`) so callers can filter/escalate it precisely
with the stdlib `warnings` filters. In each single-ticket library entry point, call
`cross_session_warning_for(ticket_id, ...)` and, when it returns a string, `warnings.warn(msg,
CrossSessionWarning, stacklevel=2)` before returning; when it returns `None`, do nothing (no
warning emitted).

Single-ticket library functions to cover (mirroring the CLI/MCP allowlist): the read
`show_ticket` (`src/rebar/_lib_reads.py:40`) and `deps`; the writes `transition` / `reopen`
(`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:272`/`:455`), `comment`, `edit`, `tag`, `untag`,
`set_file_impact`, `declare_no_file_impact`, `link` (primary endpoint), `unlink` (primary
endpoint), `archive`. Bulk reads (`list_tickets`, `search`, `ready`, `next_batch`) do **not**
warn. `claim` is excluded (an already-`in_progress` ticket raises `ConcurrencyError` before
any warning path). No function's return type changes — the warning rides the `warnings`
channel, matching the "all surfaces first-class without a return-shape change" decision.

## Scope

- A small module or the package `__init__` for the `CrossSessionWarning` category export.
- `src/rebar/_lib_reads.py` — emit in `show_ticket` and `deps`.
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` — emit in the single-ticket write functions listed above.
- `docs/reuse-surface.md` — document `rebar.CrossSessionWarning` and that single-ticket
  library functions emit it (and bulk reads do not).

## Testing

Tier: **in-process unit test** using the stdlib `warnings` capture (`pytest.warns` /
`warnings.catch_warnings(record=True)`) — the mechanism is entirely in-process
(test-design §3 pure/validation path). Real temporary tracker; acting session set via
`REBAR_SESSION_ID`.

- With a ticket held by session A and acting session B, `rebar.show_ticket(<id>)` emits
  exactly one `CrossSessionWarning` whose message names holder `A`; assert the same for one
  write, e.g. `rebar.comment(<id>, "x")`.
- Negative control (same session): acting as A, assert **no** `CrossSessionWarning` is
  emitted (`catch_warnings(record=True)` list is empty of that category).
- Bulk exclusion: `rebar.list_tickets()` / `rebar.ready()` as B emit no `CrossSessionWarning`.
- Unset-id silence: with `REBAR_SESSION_ID` unset, `rebar.show_ticket(<id>)` emits none.
- Category precision: the emitted warning is an instance of `rebar.CrossSessionWarning` (a
  `UserWarning` subclass), so a caller can filter it distinctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar.show_ticket(<id>)` and `rebar.comment(<id>, ...)` each emit exactly one
  `rebar.CrossSessionWarning` naming holder `A` when acting as session B against an A-held
  ticket (checked by a `pytest.warns` test under `make test`).
- [ ] Negative control: acting as session A, no `CrossSessionWarning` is emitted by those
  functions (checked by `catch_warnings(record=True)` asserting none of that category).
- [ ] `rebar.list_tickets()` and `rebar.ready()` as session B emit no `CrossSessionWarning`
  for A's `in_progress` ticket (checked by a bulk-exclusion assertion).
- [ ] With `REBAR_SESSION_ID` unset, `rebar.show_ticket(<id>)` emits no `CrossSessionWarning`
  (checked by an unset-id assertion).
- [ ] The emitted warning is an instance of `rebar.CrossSessionWarning` subclassing
  `UserWarning` (checked by an `isinstance` assertion in the warns test).
- [ ] `docs/reuse-surface.md` documents `rebar.CrossSessionWarning` and the single-ticket
  emission (checked: `grep -n "CrossSessionWarning" docs/reuse-surface.md` matches).
